newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pasminco says zinc outlook subdued.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pasminco says zinc outlook subdued.

text.p: Australian base metals producer Pasminco Ltd said on Wednesday that the outlook for zinc, the group's major product, remains subdued.
"Although stocks on the LME have continued to fall over the course of 1996, they remain relatively high, limiting zinc price rises," Pasminco said in a statement accompanying its annual results.
"The lead price, on the other hand, has been strong and its outlook continues to be buoyant," Pasminco said.
Pasminco said a major focus for the group was the resolution of issues surrounding the future of the Budel zinc smelter in the Netherlands.

"Despite the setback caused by the delay to RTZ-CRA's Century zinc project, Pasminco remains optimistic that a viable future for Budel Zink can be secured by the required time frame," the company said.
The Century zinc project, in Queensland, has been held up by wrangles over native land titles.
The Budel smelter's current licence requires it to halt the production of jarosite, a residue produced by the zinc process, by June 1998.
Century is one of the few zinc deposits capable of supplying the material needed to meet the deadline.
Pasminco said opportunties to expand group mine capacity would continue to be investigated during the coming year.

"Exploration at Pasminco Mining, Elura and Rosebery, continues to provide encouragement that sufficient additional resources will be proven to justify capital investment in expansion," the company said.

"In 1997 the group will continue to focus on customer service and cost and efficiency improvements, to achieve further reductions in the group's break-even zinc price, to improve competitiveness, and achieve an acceptable return for shareholders," Pasminco said.
The company earlier reported a 1995/96 net profit of A$40.8 million, up from 12.2 million a year earlier.
